outcomes.title: Number of Participants Experiencing Diarrhea
outcomes.description: Diarrhea is clinically defined as three or more loose stools per day for two consecutive days. This will be a dichotomous (yes or no) outcome of diarrhea.

outcomes.title: Adverse Events
outcomes.description: Number of reported adverse events over the duration of the study

outcomes.title: Pediatric Quality-of-life Score
outcomes.description: "The PedsQL Measurement Measurement Model for the Pediatric Quality-of-Life Inventory.~Based on the PedsQL form filled out by participants, the scores were translated using the PedsQL form guidelines: 0=100, 1=75, 2=50,3=25,4=0. The raw scores of participants were averaged after translation. The lowest possible score is 0 and the highest possible score is 100. A higher score indicates a healthier lifestyle."
outcomes.population: Some participants did not fill out the PEDSQL Day 7 form.

outcomes.title: Number of Events: Symptoms of Loose Stools, Constipation, Fever, Flatulence, Lack of Appetite, Pain, Rash, Vomiting, Cough, Earache, Nasal Congestion, Runny Nose, Sore Throat, Diarrhea.
outcomes.description: This will be a dichotomous (yes or no) outcome of loose stools, constipation, fever, flatulence, lack of appetite, pain, rash, vomiting, cough, earache, nasal congestion, runny nose, sore throat.

outcomes.title: To Assess if Probiotic Prophylaxis (BIO-K+CL1285®) is Effective for the Prevention of AAD in Hospitalized Patients.
outcomes.description: Incidence of AAD data were collected using questionnaire and diaries given to participants upon discharge. Diagnosis of AAD was made when a patient produced three or more liquid stools in a 24h period after antibiotic treatment with no other obvious reason for diarrhea.

outcomes.title: Severity of AAD in Hospitalized Patients Ingesting BIO-K+CL1285® or Placebo.
outcomes.description: Duration of diarrhea was determined by number of continuous days of diarrhea. Average number of liquid stools per day was determined by the sum of the number of liquid stools per day in the AAD episode divided by the duration of diarrhea in days.

outcomes.title: Frequency of Stool Samples Positive for Clostridium Difficile (C. Difficile) Toxin A and/or B.
outcomes.description: If diarrhea occured while hospitalized, patients provided a stool sample for C. difficile analysis of Toxin A and/or B. All episodes were recorded by a nurse of clinician on a case report form using the seven-item Bristol Stool Form Scale (Riegler et al., 2001). A diarrhea episode was described as a bowel movement consisting of watery stool with or without solids.

outcomes.title: Safety Profile of BIO-K+CL1285® Versus Placebo in Hospitalized Patients.
outcomes.description: Adverse events were reported by patients in the three study groups.

outcomes.title: Frequencies of Other Gastrointestinal Symptoms.
outcomes.description: Episodes of gastrointestinal disorders during hospitalization were recorded by patient interview and were confirmed by review of patient diaries.

To Assess if Probiotic Prophylaxis (BIO-K+CL1285®) is Effective for the Prevention of AAD in Hospitalized Patients.
outcome_measurements.description: Incidence of AAD data were collected using questionnaire and diaries given to participants upon discharge. Diagnosis of AAD was made when a patient produced three or more liquid stools in a 24h period after antibiotic treatment with no other obvious reason for diarrhea.
